# CSRNG Command Stage Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The command stage is the ingress and egress point for one CSRNG application interface. It accepts 32-bit application command words, buffers them, and forwards each command as a packetised sequence to the CSRNG command processing path. It also receives generated random data words from the processing path and returns them to the application. For generate commands, it is responsible for splitting the requested number of 128-bit blocks into a sequence of internal single-block requests, while presenting only one completion response to the application.

## 2. Reset and Enable Behavior

- After reset, the module shall be idle, all buffers empty, and all output data and response indications inactive.
- When the module is disabled, it shall not accept command words, shall ignore incoming generated data, and shall not initiate new command packet transfers or completion responses.
- When the module is disabled, any buffered command words and generated data words shall be discarded.
- The module shall return to normal operation only after being enabled and, where required, reset.

## 3. Command Input and Buffering

- The application sends commands as 32-bit words. The first word is a command header, and the header may be followed by zero or more additional data words.
- The header contains:
  - a command class;
  - a command length field, giving the number of additional 32-bit data words that follow the header;
  - command flags;
  - for generate commands, a generate length field giving the number of 128-bit random data words to be returned.
- A command word is accepted only when the module is enabled and the application and command stage both indicate that the word can be transferred.
- The command stage shall provide back-pressure: it shall indicate that it is not ready to accept a command word when its command buffer is full.
- The command buffer shall be capable of holding one maximum-length command. A maximum-length command consists of a header plus fifteen additional data words.
- The module may continue to accept and buffer command words for a new command while an earlier command is still being processed, provided buffer space is available.
- Command words shall remain in the order received.

## 4. Command Packet Transfer

- Once a command header is available, the command stage shall begin transferring that command to the downstream command consumer as a packetised sequence.
- The first word of the packet shall be marked as the start of the packet.
- If the command length is zero, the header is also the end of the packet.
- If the command length is non-zero, exactly that many additional data words shall follow the header.
- Each additional data word shall be marked as a middle-of-packet word.
- The last data word of a multi-word packet shall be marked as both middle-of-packet and end-of-packet.
- The command stage shall not end a packet before all words indicated by the command length field have been sent.
- If the command buffer has not yet received all expected data words, the command stage shall wait until they arrive before completing the packet.
- Packet boundaries shall be preserved. The command stage shall not interleave words from different commands in the same packet stream.
- The header presented to the downstream command consumer shall carry the interface/state identifier associated with this command stage, together with the command class, command length, and flags from the application header.
- The generate length field is consumed by the command stage and is not forwarded as part of the output header.
- Additional data words shall be forwarded without modification.

## 5. Command Completion and Status

- The command stage shall provide exactly one completion response to the application for each accepted command.
- For non-generate commands, the completion response shall be generated after the downstream command consumer acknowledges the forwarded command.
- The completion response shall include the status supplied by the downstream command consumer.
- The module shall not interpret the status; it shall forward the status value unchanged.
- The completion response shall be a single-cycle indication, accompanied by the associated status in the same cycle.

## 6. Generate Command Handling

- A generate command is recognised from the command class field in the header.
- The generate length field indicates how many 128-bit generated data words the application expects to receive.
- The initial command packet, including any optional data words, shall be sent to the downstream command consumer as the first internal request.
- After the first internal request is acknowledged, if more generated blocks remain, the command stage shall issue an additional internal generate request.
- Each additional internal generate request shall be a short packet marked as both start-of-packet and end-of-packet.
- Each subsequent request shall carry the same interface/state identifier, command class, command length, and flags as the original generate command.
- The command stage shall repeat this process until the full generate length has been satisfied.
- The command stage shall not issue the next internal generate request until the previous generated data word has been accepted by the application and the generated-data buffer has space.
- The application completion response for a generate command shall be generated only after:
  - all internal generate requests have been acknowledged by the downstream command consumer, and
  - all generated data words have been delivered to the application.
- The status reported to the application shall be the status associated with the final internal acknowledgment.

## 7. Generated Bits Output

- For each internal generate request, the command stage shall receive one 128-bit generated data word.
- Each generated data word shall be accompanied by a compliance flag, indicating whether the data was produced in a FIPS-compliant manner.
- The command stage shall buffer at most one generated data word at a time.
- The module shall indicate when a generated data word is available to the application.
- The application may apply back-pressure when it is not ready to receive generated data.
- A generated data word is considered delivered when the module indicates it is valid and the application indicates it is ready.
- The compliance flag shall be presented together with its associated generated data word and shall be passed through unchanged.
- Generated data words shall be delivered in the order produced.
- No generated data word shall be dropped, duplicated, or reordered.

## 8. Error Indications

- The command stage shall provide error indications for abnormal buffer conditions.
- A command-buffer error shall be indicated if a command word is written when the command buffer is full, read when it is empty, or if the buffer reports an inconsistent full/empty state.
- A generated-data-buffer error shall be indicated if a generated data word is written when the buffer is full, read when it is empty, or if the buffer reports an inconsistent full/empty state.
- The command stage shall provide a control error indication.
- If the internal control logic reaches an illegal or unrecognised state, the module shall assert the control error indication and halt further processing. Normal operation shall only resume after reset.
